summary: Three independent runs exercised the backend and frontend successfully. The union found one critical booking-state race: two overlapping pending bookings can both be confirmed because overlap is checked at creation and not again during confirmation. Minor findings are that non-zero-padded dates such as 2099-1-01 are accepted despite the documented YYYY-MM-DD contract, and the external email provider was rate-limited during repeated submissions; the app persisted records and returned success while notification delivery failed. All requested core API, availability, status, navigation, home, stays, booking-modal, and contact-modal flows were otherwise reachable and working; run 3 noted the pristine preloader could not be asserted because the shared browser session had already visited.

critical.title: Confirming a pending overlapping booking is allowed
critical.steps_to_reproduce: 1. POST /api/bookings for a unique stay with dates 2026-12-05 through 2026-12-08; response is 201/requested. 2. POST a second booking for the same stay with overlapping dates 2026-12-06 through 2026-12-09; response is also 201/requested because only confirmed bookings are checked at create time. 3. Confirm the first booking with POST /api/bookings/{id}/status and status=confirmed. 4. Confirm the second booking.
critical.expected: The second confirmation should be rejected with 409, or otherwise remain unconfirmed, because its dates overlap an existing confirmed reservation.
critical.actual: The second status update returns 200 and status=confirmed, leaving two overlapping confirmed reservations for the same stay.
critical.impact: The booking system can double-book a stay whenever overlapping requests are created before either is confirmed; availability and the UI can report an invalid inventory state.

minor.title: Booking API accepts non-YYYY-MM-DD dates
minor.steps_to_reproduce: POST /api/bookings with a valid payload except check_in=2099-1-01 and check_out=2099-11-03, or another valid later date using an unpadded month/day format.
minor.expected: Because the API contract specifies YYYY-MM-DD, the request should return HTTP 422 for the unpadded format.
minor.actual: The request returns HTTP 201 and persists the booking; datetime.strptime accepts the non-zero-padded format because the model fields are strings and the endpoint has no strict regex/date-format check.
minor.impact: Clients can persist inconsistent date representations, which can undermine string-based overlap comparisons and produce inconsistent availability data.

minor.title: Email provider rate limiting observed during repeated UI submissions
minor.location: POST /api/inquiries and POST /api/bookings email notification path
minor.steps_to_reproduce: Submit several inquiry and booking requests in close succession while exercising the public app, including the shared concurrent regression runs; inspect backend.err.log or the integration response.
minor.expected: The notification send should succeed or be retried/queued while the inquiry or booking request remains successful.
minor.actual: The first notification requests succeeded or returned 202, but subsequent calls received 429 rate_limited from integrations.emergentagent.com. The handlers caught the exception, persisted the records, and still returned 201; logs reported that email notification failed.
minor.impact: Inquiry and booking data is retained, but owner email notifications may not be delivered after the provider rate limit is reached. This was intermittent and may be a shared external/provider quota issue rather than deterministic application logic.
